cards.source: REF 5.1 (india_ideology.jpg) recovers the question and the answer 'No. Hit us first and you'll breathe your last.' on the SUPREMO side; the opposite side is authored here because only one face was ever legible. REF 2.4 records that zero ordinary question cards were recovered in full. 2026-10-05: authored side rewritten for clarity; recovered text unchanged.
cards.question: Do you condemn the use of surgical strikes as a reactionary tool?

sides.answer: No. Hit us first and you'll breathe your last.
Yes. Strikes staged for votes risk a war that ordinary soldiers must fight.

cards.source: REF 5.2 verifies the Capitalist side of the shipped 'SHOULD WE INVADE NEW SPAIN?' card pays 2 Trust + 1 Media and ZERO Funds, and REF 8.1 recovers the 'far more lucrative to invade nearby islands' answer. The Supremo side is authored; the ideologue of the recovered answer is inferred from its reasoning. 2026-10-05: authored side rewritten for clarity; recovered text unchanged.
cards.question: Should we invade New Spain?

sides.answer: No. It would be far more lucrative to invade nearby islands and expand our fishing territories.
Yes. A nation that never expands its borders is a nation waiting to shrink.

cards.source: REF 8.1 question 3, recovered from the official 432-card marketing render. No answer side was legible; both answers are authored in the REF 8.2 register. 2026-10-05: authored side rewritten for clarity; recovered text unchanged.
cards.question: Should mistakes be forgiven?

sides.answer: No. Forgive one unpaid loan and every borrower learns repayment is optional.
Yes. People who admit their mistakes deserve a second chance, not lifelong punishment.

cards.source: REF 8.1 question 4, recovered from the official 432-card marketing render. No answer side was legible; both answers are authored in the REF 8.2 register. 2026-10-05: authored side rewritten for clarity; recovered text unchanged.
cards.question: Should women be free to have children single or in a relationship?

sides.answer: Yes. Whether to raise a child alone is her choice, not the state's.
No. Most voters are not ready for it, and unpopular causes lose elections.

cards.source: REF 8.1 question 5, recovered from the official 432-card marketing render. No answer side was legible; both answers are authored in the REF 8.2 register. 2026-10-05: authored side rewritten for clarity; recovered text unchanged.
cards.question: Should the government spend money on space exploration?

sides.answer: Yes. Space research inspires every child in every village classroom to study science.
No. A rocket launch is a one-day headline; potholes make headlines every monsoon.

cards.source: REF 8.1 question 6, recovered from the official 432-card marketing render. No answer side was legible; both answers are authored in the REF 8.2 register. REBALANCED for D2: side 1 paid {media 2, funds 1} against side 0's {trust 2, funds 2}, a visible ONE-RESOURCE total edge the old tolerance band swallowed, so one answer was never right under full information. Side 1 now pays {media 2, funds 2}; the two compositions stay incomparable. See BALANCE_TOLERANCE_TOTAL in src/balance.ts. 2026-10-05: authored side rewritten for clarity; recovered text unchanged.
cards.question: Is providing free food, housing and healthcare to all citizens a good idea?

sides.answer: Yes. Food, a roof and medicine are basic rights, not rewards.
No. Promise it all and every shortage becomes tomorrow's front page.

cards.source: REF 8.1 question 7, recovered from the official 432-card marketing render. No answer side was legible; both answers are authored in the REF 8.2 register. 2026-10-05: authored side rewritten for clarity; recovered text unchanged.
cards.question: Do the poor have the right to take wealth from the rich?

sides.answer: No. Seize wealth once and investors take their money elsewhere for good.
Yes. The power of a nation lies with its masses, not its millionaires.

cards.source: REF 8.1 question 8, recovered from the official 432-card marketing render. No answer side was legible; both answers are authored in the REF 8.2 register. 2026-10-05: authored side rewritten for clarity; recovered text unchanged.
cards.question: Should the rich be taxed to fund free higher education?

sides.answer: Yes. Talent is everywhere in the country, but tuition money is not.
No. Heavy taxes drive away the very earners who create graduate jobs.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2 (deadpan, Yes./No. opener, no jokes in the answer). Added because the recovered question pool is eight cards deep and one deck cannot show a fourth of the pairing table. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Can parties hand out free laptops and televisions before an election?

sides.answer: Yes. Nothing fills a rally ground like a free television on the stage.
No. Election freebies are paid for with borrowed money and future taxes.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. REF 2.3 infers from 14 tournament hands that Idealist and Supremo sit in largely disjoint question space; this card tests the seam rather than filling it. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Do police need a judge's warrant to tap a citizen's phone?

sides.answer: No. Waiting for a judge gives criminals time to switch their phones.
Yes. Without a warrant, every critic's private calls become the state's business.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Added to cover the Showstopper x Supremo pairing, which the recovered question pool never exercises. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Can authorities shut down mobile internet during riots?

sides.answer: Yes. Cutting the network stops rumours before they turn into mobs.
No. A blackout becomes the biggest headline of all, here and abroad.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Added so the Capitalist x Supremo pair is not carried entirely by the two recovered New Spain / wealth answers. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Must the army buy its weapons only from Indian factories?

sides.answer: No. Foreign suppliers are often cheaper and faster, and the budget is limited.
Yes. A country that imports its weapons can be switched off by others.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. REF 8.2 rule 3 (question at most 12 words, answer at most 15 after the Yes/No) is the authoring constraint here; the situation carries the satire and the wording stays flat. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Do elected ministers deserve the final say on appointing high court judges?

sides.answer: No. Investors trust contracts only where judges are free of political pressure.
Yes. Elected leaders, not unelected judges, should hold that power.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. The recovered question pool contains no procurement question at all, which is the register's largest silence. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Can farmers sell crops to private traders outside government mandis?

sides.answer: Yes. More buyers mean better prices for farmers and less wasted grain.
No. The mandi system keeps the nation's food supply under firm state control.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Is fencing every kilometre of the eastern border worth the cost?

sides.answer: No. The money would earn far more spent on trade posts than fences.
Yes. A border you cannot see is a border you cannot hold.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. SIDE 1 REWRITTEN 2026-10-04: it read "No. Digitise it now and the next sale is fast enough to be invisible.", which told the reader to DO the thing its own "No" rejected, so the two sides advocated one action and the polarity token was the only difference. Nothing was dropped: the clause about the sale being fast enough to be invisible is retained, re-argued as the cost of digitising rather than as a reason to digitise. See decks/SOURCES.md. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Does the Centre need its power to dismiss elected state governments?

sides.answer: No. Investors flee states where an elected government can vanish overnight.
Yes. When a state slides into disorder, the Centre must be able to step in.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Welfare questions recovered at REF 8.1 items 6 and 8 are all-or-nothing; this one is about the boundary of a scheme that already exists. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Must households pay for every litre of piped water they use?

sides.answer: Yes. Free water gets wasted, while metered water pays for the pipes.
No. Clean drinking water belongs to everyone, not just to those who can pay.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Should the pension age rise with life expectancy?

sides.answer: Yes. Longer lives on the same retirement age will bankrupt the pension fund.
No. Labourers who started work at fourteen should not toil until seventy.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Do World Cup cricket matches belong on free public television?

sides.answer: No. Broadcast rights are worth billions, and free telecasts wipe out that value.
Yes. A free World Cup final puts the whole country before one screen.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. REF 8.2 rule 4 forbids a joke in the answer; the joke here is entirely in the situation. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Do campaigns need to go silent on social media before polling day?

sides.answer: Yes. A quiet period stops parties outspending each other on last-minute ads.
No. The final two days are when one viral video wins the seat.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Is it proper for public money to buy ads praising government schemes?

sides.answer: No. Crores spent on self-praise build nothing and return nothing.
Yes. A scheme nobody has heard of is a scheme nobody votes for.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Can police ban a protest without first going to court?

sides.answer: Yes. Officers on the ground know when a crowd is about to turn violent.
No. The right to protest means nothing if police can cancel it at will.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. REF 8.2 rule 8 permits references to real subjects; no individual is named, the question is the register's ordinary register of consequence rather than of person. SIDE 0 REWRITTEN 2026-10-04: it read "No. Publish it and the next recruitment is only a rumour.", which told the reader to publish the name its own "No" refused. Nothing was dropped: the clause about the next recruitment being only a rumour is retained and re-argued as the cost of the list rather than as an instruction to build one. See decks/SOURCES.md. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Must every young citizen do a year of military service?

sides.answer: Yes. A year in uniform builds discipline and a stronger nation.
No. Forcing young people to carry weapons violates their freedom of conscience.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Do news channels deserve fines for airing fake news?

sides.answer: Yes. Lies on air spark riots, and the state must keep order.
No. Fines make channels timid, and timid news gets no viewers.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Must police officers wear body cameras on every shift?

sides.answer: No. Officers who feel watched hesitate, and hesitation in a crisis costs lives.
Yes. One clip of an officer doing right beats a thousand press releases.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Do political rallies have the right to block main city roads?

sides.answer: No. Roads belong to ambulances and commuters, not to whoever brings the biggest crowd.
Yes. A rally nobody sees from the main road is a rally wasted.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. REF 8.2 rule 7 requires campaign variety; this is the enumeration question the recovered pool never reaches. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Is compulsory voting a good idea for national elections?

sides.answer: No. Forcing people to vote punishes the poorest, who cannot miss a day's wages.
Yes. Record turnout makes a dazzling headline for the world's largest democracy.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Can criminal trials be broadcast live on national television?

sides.answer: No. Cameras turn witnesses into performers and victims into entertainment.
Yes. Live trials would draw bigger audiences than any prime-time serial.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. SIDE 1 REWRITTEN 2026-10-04: it read "No. Name the schools and the parents read nothing else.", which told the reader to name the schools its own "No" refused. Nothing was dropped: the clause about the parents reading nothing else is retained, re-argued as the risk of naming rather than as a reason to name. See decks/SOURCES.md. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Must riverfront beautification wait until the river itself is clean?

sides.answer: Yes. Clean water for people downstream matters more than a pretty riverside walk.
No. A gleaming riverfront is the photograph that wins the next election.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Is it right for police to parade arrested suspects before the press?

sides.answer: No. A suspect is innocent until convicted, not a prop for photographers.
Yes. A suspect paraded before cameras shows the public that police are working.

cards.source: REF 8.1 item 9 recovers the stem 'SHOULD WE [STOP] AERIAL BOMBING DEVELOPED COUNTRIES?' legible in the official 432-card marketing render, but the verb is bracketed by the researcher as an inference and REF 8.1 says explicitly: do not treat as verbatim. MISSING CLAUSE: one word, the verb, which is supplied here. No answer side was legible at all; both answers are authored in the REF 8.2 register. 2026-10-05: authored side rewritten for clarity; recovered text unchanged.
cards.question: Should we stop aerial bombing developed countries?

sides.answer: No. Wartime orders keep our arms factories busy and our workers paid.
Yes. Every bombed city on the evening news makes us look like villains.

cards.source: REF 8.1 item 10 recovers the stem 'SHOULD KASHMIRI FARMERS BE GIVEN THE RIGHT TO FLY [â€¦]?' legible only up to the word FLY; REF 8.1 says explicitly: do not treat as verbatim. MISSING CLAUSE: the object of 'fly' â€” 'drones' is supplied here and is authored, not recovered. No answer side was legible at all; both answers are authored in the REF 8.2 register. 2026-10-05: authored side rewritten for clarity; recovered text unchanged.
cards.question: Should Kashmiri farmers be given the right to fly drones?

sides.answer: No. Unregistered drones near a sensitive border are a security risk, whoever flies them.
Yes. Kashmiri farmers deserve the same farm technology as farmers everywhere else.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Authored to open the register's smallest scale. REF 2.3 infers the recovered question pool is entirely national and international in framing; no recovered card concerns a village panchayat, a water right or a local allocation, so the deck had no small-scale question at all. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Are big dams worth building if they flood tribal villages?

sides.answer: Yes. One dam powers millions of homes and irrigates whole districts.
No. Tribal families lose homes, forests and graves for someone else's electricity.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. A creditor-versus-debtor question. The recovered pool contains one wealth question (REF 8.1 item 7) and one taxation question (item 8) and no question about who absorbs a loss already booked, which is a different trade. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Is a farm loan waiver justified after a failed monsoon?

sides.answer: No. Waivers teach borrowers to wait for the next election instead of repaying.
Yes. A farmer ruined by drought should not lose his land as well.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Authored to put the two sides on opposite sides of an international obligation, where the recovered pool's only non-domestic questions are about invading and bombing other countries. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Should India pay more than its agreed share of the climate fund?

sides.answer: No. Every extra rupee sent abroad is a rupee not invested at home.
Yes. Climate change hits the poorest first, and they cannot wait for fair shares.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Authored because the recovered welfare questions (REF 8.1 items 6 and 8) are all about whether a benefit exists, and none about who inside the household is measured by it. The Capitalist side is the restrained one here, which is the deck's answer to a greedy side reading as the obvious one. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Can private companies run prisons for profit?

sides.answer: Yes. Private operators build cells faster and run them for less.
No. Nobody should profit from keeping more people locked up for longer.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. The incumbent-hedging question. REF 8.1 recovers campaign questions from the American material; the recovered pool contains no question about the timing advantage of the party already in office. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Can companies fund political parties anonymously through electoral bonds?

sides.answer: Yes. Anonymous donors give more because they need not fear business reprisals.
No. Secret donations look shady, and voters punish parties that look shady.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. REF 8.1 item 5 is the only recovered question about spending, and it asks about space. This asks about the ordinary recurring purchase every district makes, where visibility and price pull in opposite directions. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Is selling naming rights to metro stations a good idea?

sides.answer: Yes. Naming rights pay for maintenance without raising a single fare.
No. A station named after a soap brand becomes a national joke.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. The land question. ig-in2020-016 asks whether land records should be digitised; nothing in the recovered pool asks what happens to the ground once they are. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Can farmland be taken for factories without the farmers' consent?

sides.answer: Yes. One big factory creates more jobs than a hundred small farms.
No. Taking land without consent is theft, whatever the compensation.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. The inter-generational question, which the recovered pool has no instance of at all: every recovered card decides something inside one electoral term. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Is opening coal mines in protected forests worth the extra power?

sides.answer: Yes. Cheap coal keeps the factories running and the lights on.
No. An ancient forest cannot be replanted once the mine is exhausted.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Transparency with a price on it. The Capitalist side is the one that votes to keep a file closed, so the question does not reward the reflex of its own answer. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Must TV channels limit advertising to ten minutes an hour?

sides.answer: No. Ad revenue keeps channels alive, and a cap would bankrupt half of them.
Yes. Fewer ad breaks keep viewers glued instead of reaching for the remote.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Extends the procurement family of ig-in2020-013 and ig-in2020-014 from the price of the work to the name on the envelope. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Must exit polls stay secret until the last vote is cast?

sides.answer: Yes. Early exit polls swing the stock market on guesses, not results.
No. Exit polls make election night the most watched television of the year.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Both sides here are defensible and neither is cheap, which is the register's ordinary shape: two spends competing for one season. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Can troops be sent into a riot-hit state without its consent?

sides.answer: No. Soldiers on city streets scare off investors for years.
Yes. Order comes first, and a state that lost control has no veto.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Sovereignty against cost. The Capitalist side is the one that opens the tender to a foreign firm, so the greedy reading of the Ideologue and the cautious reading coincide on this card. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Can a foreign company bid to run a major Indian port?

sides.answer: Yes. Open bidding brings the lowest price and the best technology.
No. A strategic port in foreign hands is a gate we cannot lock.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Disclosure of a number that the state controls. The recovered pool contains no question about a published statistic, which is the ordinary instrument of the register. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Should the district hospital publish its death rate every quarter?

sides.answer: Yes. Patients have a right to know how safe their hospital is.
No. One bad quarter becomes a scandal that drives patients away.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Eligibility rather than existence. ig-in2020-017 asks whether a scheme should reach further geographically; this asks whether it should be universal or means-tested, which is the same money for a different named group. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Must police register every complaint they receive as an FIR?

sides.answer: Yes. A complaint turned away at the station is justice denied at the door.
No. Registering every complaint makes the crime figures look terrible.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Language policy. Neither recovered welfare question nor any of the eight recovered stems asks who has to be addressed in what language to receive a benefit. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Must Hindi be taught in schools in every state?

sides.answer: No. Each state's own language deserves equal respect in its classrooms.
Yes. One shared language builds one national audience for every message.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Extends the transparency family of ig-in2020-016 and ig-in2020-041 from records to money actually moved, and both sides agree the deadline is correct and disagree about whether it has force. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Must every rupee sent to village panchayats be published online?

sides.answer: Yes. Villagers deserve to see exactly where their development money goes.
No. Every misspent rupee would become a local scandal by morning.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Two constituencies with incompatible reasons, which is the register's preferred shape: both sides are defending somebody, neither is defending a self-interest. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Should the Centre impose final settlements on interstate river disputes?

sides.answer: No. Farmers in each state deserve a fair hearing, not a decree from Delhi.
Yes. Only a firm central hand can end decades of state quarrels.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Borders. REF 2.3 [INFERRED] that Idealist and Supremo sit in largely disjoint question space, and ig-in2020-001 and ig-in2020-032 already touch the seam; this is the fourth card on it and the first that asks who an administrative line is drawn for. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Should slum families be rehoused on the same land before demolition?

sides.answer: Yes. Families who built the city should not be pushed to its edge.
No. City land follows the master plan, and the plan cannot bend for encroachers.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. An unprofitable service. The recovered pool has no question about whether to keep running something that loses money, which is the ordinary form of most state expenditure. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Should loss-making rural bus routes keep running at public expense?

sides.answer: Yes. For many villages, that bus is the only road to a hospital.
No. A strong nation spends on expressways, not on half-empty buses.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. The courts. REF 8.1 recovers no institutional question at all, and a deadline imposed on an institution that does not control its backlog is the register's sharpest ordinary dilemma. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Should each new government be free to rewrite school history textbooks?

sides.answer: No. History belongs to the evidence, not to whoever won the last election.
Yes. Children should learn the story the nation chooses to tell.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Broadcast form as a question. The recovered Showstopper questions are all about whether to say something; this one is about where it is said, which the cut decides for you. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Should the national cricket team refuse matches against hostile neighbours?

sides.answer: No. A rivalry match draws the biggest television audience of the year.
Yes. No trophy is worth more than the country's honour.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. Internal party discipline. Extends ig-in2020-037 from the calendar advantage of the incumbent to whether its own members are countable in public, which is a different institutional question. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Should the film censor board be allowed to order scene cuts?

sides.answer: No. Every cut scene becomes the clip the whole country searches for.
Yes. Someone has to decide what the nation's screens are fit to show.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. The distribution question that every recovered card abstains from: not whether to build something but which district it goes in. The Showstopper side is the one arguing for the minister's own district, so the patronage reading is not automatically the greedy side. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Should new government doctors be required to serve two years in villages?

sides.answer: No. Clips of furious young doctors on strike would drown out any good news.
Yes. Doctors trained on public money owe the nation their service.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2. A one-month bilateral concession, which is the register's preferred shape: both sides can be defended, and the disagreement is entirely about what a precedent is worth. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Should loudspeaker noise limits apply during religious festivals too?

sides.answer: No. Nobody ever won a crowd by turning down a festival's music.
Yes. One rule for every faith keeps order on every street.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2, tone per REF 5. Dropped: the card's second printed face (REF 5.3) and its ideologue nameplate. Capitalist on who pays for the cold chain, Supremo on the admission a ration concedes. REF 5.1 prints no condition, no seat-relative direction and no effect clause, so none is dropped here. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Should foreign tech companies be forced to store Indian users' data locally?

sides.answer: No. Local data centres raise costs and scare away foreign investment.
Yes. Data about our citizens belongs under our own laws.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2, tone per REF 5. Dropped: second printed face (REF 5.3) and the ideologue nameplate. Capitalist on grain that cannot move, Supremo on what trade concedes about sovereignty. REF 5.1 prints no condition or effect clause, so none is dropped. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Should investors from bordering countries need government approval to buy Indian firms?

sides.answer: No. Startups need every rupee they can raise, whatever its passport.
Yes. Whoever owns our companies can pull our strings in a crisis.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2, tone per REF 5. Dropped: second printed face (REF 5.3) and the ideologue nameplate. Capitalist on the bed already paid for, Supremo on what an unfilled ward is evidence of. REF 5.1 prints no condition or effect clause, so none is dropped. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Should cash payments above two lakh rupees be banned outright?

sides.answer: No. Small traders run on cash, and a ban slows the whole market.
Yes. Cash is where black money hides from the state.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2, tone per REF 5. Dropped: second printed face (REF 5.3) and the ideologue nameplate. Capitalist on arrears becoming custom, Supremo on the state naming the month it chooses to hurt. REF 5.1 prints no condition or effect clause, so none is dropped. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Should diesel cars over ten years old be banned from Delhi?

sides.answer: No. A ban wipes out family savings and hurts the auto industry.
Yes. A capital choking on smoke is an embarrassment to the nation.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2, tone per REF 5. Dropped: second printed face (REF 5.3) and the ideologue nameplate. Capitalist on a party that raises its own money, Supremo on what a party that cannot is owned by. REF 5.1 prints no condition or effect clause, so none is dropped. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Should private companies reserve most jobs for residents of their state?

sides.answer: No. Firms grow by hiring the best worker, wherever they were born.
Yes. Local jobs for local youth keep the streets calm and loyal.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2, tone per REF 5. Dropped: second printed face (REF 5.3) and the ideologue nameplate. Capitalist on scarcity clearing, Showstopper on the hour a shortage is said at. REF 5.1 prints no condition or effect clause, so none is dropped. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Should private hospital fees be capped during a pandemic?

sides.answer: No. Price caps push hospitals to turn away patients they cannot afford.
Yes. Nothing looks worse than a family's hospital bill going viral.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2, tone per REF 5. Dropped: second printed face (REF 5.3) and the ideologue nameplate. Capitalist on the settled location fee, Showstopper on who is asked to watch the premiere. REF 5.1 prints no condition or effect clause, so none is dropped. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.
cards.question: Should cinemas have to play the national anthem before every film?

sides.answer: No. Audiences pay for the film, and theatres should sell what they pay for.
Yes. A packed hall standing together makes a powerful picture.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2, tone per REF 5. Dropped: second printed face (REF 5.3) and the ideologue nameplate. Capitalist on what the cover price is buying, Showstopper on a paper reduced to a noticeboard. REF 5.1 prints no condition or effect clause, so none is dropped. 2026-10-05: rewritten for clarity.

No. Only the state holds the gun; that is what order means.

cards.question: Should bull-taming sports like Jallikattu stay legal?

sides.answer: No. Hospital bills and insurance claims outweigh a few days of festival trade.
Yes. Nothing pulls a live television audience like a charging bull.

sides.answer: Yes. Private trusts would run temple estates far more profitably than babus.
No. State boards appoint priests of every caste; private trusts may not.
